name: Trader Dashboard
description: A personal workbench for planning, testing and practising day trades, built around hard risk limits.
tagline: A personal workbench for planning, testing and practising day trades, built around hard risk limits.
body:
Trader Dashboard is a tool we built for our own use. It runs on one Windows PC and takes a day trade through fixed steps: scan the market for setups, check the news, wait for the entry signal, set the stop and the target before buying, replay the trade against the stock's own history, size the position to the budget, and run a risk check. Each step writes a file that the next one reads, so every decision can be traced afterwards.

The risk check comes before everything else. A trade with no stop, a loss at the stop larger than the limit per trade, too little reward for the risk, or a day that has already used its loss limit is blocked, and the reason is shown. Getting out of a trade is never blocked.

It only trades practice money: a built-in simulator and an Alpaca paper account. Nothing is sent without a click, and the autopilot only proposes trades. It shows its reasoning and waits for Accept or Deny.

This is a personal software project. It is not investment advice, and SRATH does not offer it, or any trading or advisory service, to anyone.
features: The trade in steps: scan, news, entry signal, exit plan, replay, sizing, risk check
Risk check that blocks any trade over the limits and says why
Replay a past trading day bar by bar, with the future and later news hidden
Strategy tests that pick on some months and check on later ones, with a final set kept aside
Autopilot that proposes trades and waits for a yes
Simulator and Alpaca paper trading only. Real money is not connected
tech: Python: a local web server on 127.0.0.1, standard library only
JavaScript: the dashboard itself, no framework
Alpaca API: paper trading account and price history
Yahoo Finance and SEC EDGAR: free prices, headlines and company filings
Claude Code skills: scanner, entry, exit, sizing and risk steps
